page.text:
A *group homomorphism* is a mapping between groups that preserves
algebraic structure: $\varphi(a *_1 b) = \varphi(a) *_2 \varphi(b)$.
Homomorphisms are the structure-preserving conduits through which groups
are compared, classified, and represented.

A homomorphism is an *isomorphism* if it is bijective, in which case the
two groups possess identical abstract algebraic structures. An
isomorphism from a group to itself is an *automorphism*; the set of all
automorphisms of $G$ forms a group $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ under function
composition.
